result:
Both gates pass: `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` reports 21 pass / 0 fail (the stack trace in the output is the pre-existing PostController search test logging an expected 422).

**Summary**

I moved all `/login` and `/register` copy into the translation catalogs and added a Japanese one. `lang/en/auth.json` now holds the two pages' English strings verbatim under `auth.login.*` / `auth.register.*` keys, `lang/ja/auth.json` mirrors it key-for-key with the requested Japanese wording, and `lang/ja/messages.json` translates the existing welcome message as `":nameへようこそ！"` with its placeholder intact (`bunx guren check --i18n` reports full 20-key parity on both locales). `src/app.ts` now declares `i18n: { supported: ['en', 'ja'] }`, so the framework's locale-detection middleware resolves `ja`/`ja-JP`/`ja-JP,ja;q=0.9,en-US;q=0.8,en;q=0.7` to Japanese while a missing header, English, English-outranks-Japanese, and unsupported-only headers all fall back to English. `resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx` and `Register.tsx` now pull every label, heading, subtitle, button, footer line, and `<Head title>` from `useTranslation()` instead of hardcoded text (markup, form fields, validation-error rendering and submit targets untouched), and `LoginController.show()` / `RegisterController.show()` pass `this.t('auth.<page>.title')` as the server-rendered document title so the tab title is localized before hydration too. `.guren/translations.gen.ts` was regenerated for the new typed keys. New `tests/AuthLocalization.test.ts` server-renders both pages through the same path `resources/js/ssr.tsx` uses, asserting the exact Japanese strings for Japanese `Accept-Language` values and the unchanged English strings for every other case, plus catalog key/placeholder parity.
